facts.label: Strongest contrary evidence and limitations
facts.text: - Subsequent event is incomplete. The TopBuild closing date is after the balance sheet date, and the filing says: page:26: "initial accounting for the business combination is incomplete and the Company is not yet able to disclose the provisional amounts". Mechanism: the June 30 balance sheet shows escrowed proceeds as restricted cash, page:8 of the August release footnote: "restricted cash of $3.0 billion, representing the gross proceeds from the issuance of the 6.500% Senior Notes due 2031 and 6.875% Senior Notes due 2034". Debt, preferred stock, shares and earnings capacity after July 1, 2026 therefore sit outside the reported balance sheet. Consequence: any leverage or liquidity measure built on June 30, 2026 figures mixes a pre-closing balance sheet with a financing that closed on July 1, 2026, and downstream modules must show a pro forma debt bridge from narrative only and label it as constructed. - Perimeter changes. QXO was a software and services company before Beacon: 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl page:18: "the financial results of QXO as of and for any periods prior to April 29, 2025 do not include the financial results of Beacon". Beacon was determined the predecessor (page:12). The pack carries no complete Beacon predecessor statements: page:98: "The predecessor financial information is included as Exhibit 99.1 to this Quarterly Report and is incorporated herein by reference" and the exhibit index (page:99) shows it as a prior filing, not in the pack. Consequence: FY2025 and first-half 2025 comparatives are not like-for-like with 2026, and Kodiak contributes only from April 1, 2026 (August release page:1: "from the date of acquisition on April 1, 2026"). Trailing twelve-month figures would blend four different perimeters. - Mid-year presentation change. 10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl page:12 records that rounding changed in the second quarter of 2026 to the nearest whole million, while earlier filings and the February and May releases show one decimal. Conflict locators: May release page:1 "$ 1,730.2" versus August release page:1 "$ 4,976". Consequence: sums across periods can differ by rounding; this is a presentation difference, not a restatement, and no restatement was found by a search for restatement language beyond the cover check box. - Executed documents absent. The exhibit list shows the indentures, supplemental indentures and the incremental term loan amendment as filed exhibits (10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl page:98 and page:99) but none is in the pack. Consequence: covenant definitions, baskets, restricted payment tests, guarantor lists and change-of-control terms are known only through the note summaries. The filing says restrictions are not significant for common dividends (page:51), which is a management statement. - No presentation or Q3 2026 results. No investor deck and no results for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 are in the pack, and the Q2 10-Q says the preliminary TopBuild purchase price allocation is expected in the September 2026 quarter report. Whether that report was available before the cutoff is not evidenced by the pack; nothing after the cutoff is assumed. - Management claims. Market-position and target statements (for example the "$50 billion in annual revenue within the decade" target) are management assertions in the releases (August release page:2), not filed fact; non-GAAP measures carry management add-backs (restructuring, transaction, transformation, stock-based compensation) that need reconciliation to filed figures downstream.

facts.label: Financial base view
facts.text: The reported base supports a clear picture through June 30, 2026 and a bounded one after it. Through March 31, 2026 the group had 3,100.0 of borrowings (a term loan and secured notes), no drawing on its asset-based revolver, and cash almost equal to borrowings, so net debt was small. During the second quarter it bought Kodiak with preferred equity and shares, and in June it sold 3,000 of new notes whose proceeds sat in escrow until TopBuild closed on July 1, 2026. The June 30 balance sheet therefore shows borrowings of 6,111 but also 3,000 of restricted cash that is not counted in liquidity. After closing there are a further 3,000 incremental term loan and 1,000 of Series C preferred stock, which are reported only as subsequent events. Earnings are measured on company-defined Adjusted EBITDA, which excludes TopBuild, includes Kodiak only from April 1, 2026, and adds back stock compensation, restructuring, transaction, transformation and inventory fair value items. Seasonality is strong: the first quarter earns almost nothing and the half-year cash flow from operations is negative. Every ratio below is therefore labelled with its perimeter and is not a pro forma figure.

During the second quarter it bought Kodiak with preferred equity and shares, and in June it sold 3,000 of new notes whose proceeds sat in escrow until TopBuild closed on July 1, 2026. The June 30 balance sheet therefore shows borrowings of 6,111 but also 3,000 of restricted cash that is not counted in liquidity. After closing there are a further 3,000 incremental term loan and 1,000 of Series C preferred stock, which are reported only as subsequent events. Earnings are measured on company-defined Adjusted EBITDA, which excludes TopBuild, includes Kodiak only from April 1, 2026, and adds back stock compensation, restructuring, transaction, transformation and inventory fair value items. Seasonality is strong: the first quarter earns almost nothing and the half-year cash flow from operations is negative. Every ratio below is therefore labelled with its perimeter and is not a pro forma figure.

facts.label: Covenants
facts.text: Maintenance covenants: the only financial maintenance test described is the ABL springing fixed charge coverage ratio of 1.0 to 1.0, applicable when availability is below the greater of 120 and 10% of the lesser of the borrowing base and commitments. The reported figure of the ratio is not supplied. Headroom is on the trigger: availability of 1,930 against a trigger of at most 200 (see Calculations), so the test is not currently live. Indentures and credit agreements contain customary covenants and the issuer states compliance at June 30, 2026. Definitions, baskets and incurrence ratios are not supplied; the executed documents are not in the pack. Restricted payments, including common dividends, are limited; the company says the limits are not significant given its intention not to pay common dividends, and the effect on preferred dividends is not stated.

facts.label: Calculations
facts.text: 1. LTM Adjusted EBITDA at June 30, 2026 = FY2025 647.8 + H1 2026 273 - H1 2025 196 = 724.8. LTM at March 31, 2026 = 647.8 + 1.2 - (-9.0) = 658.0. Check on H1 2025: Q1 2025 (-9.0) plus Q2 2025 (204) = 195 against 196 printed, a rounding difference. 2. Borrowings principal at June 30, 2026 = long-term debt principal 6,100 (850 + 1,500 + 2,250 + 1,500) + ABL 11 = 6,111. At December 31, 2025 and March 31, 2026 = 850.0 + 2,250.0 = 3,100.0. 3. Net debt = principal less unrestricted cash: December 2025 3,100.0 - 2,361.6 = 738.4; March 2026 3,100.0 - 3,046.3 = 53.7; June 2026 6,111 - 2,774 = 3,337. If the 3,000 escrow were treated as cash, June net debt would be 337, but that cash was committed to the purchase and released July 1, 2026. 4. Ratios: 3,100.0 / 647.8 = 4.79; 738.4 / 647.8 = 1.14; 3,100.0 / 658.0 = 4.71; 53.7 / 658.0 = 0.08; 6,111 / 724.8 = 8.43; 3,337 / 724.8 = 4.60. 5. Cash interest LTM at June 30, 2026 = 138.0 + 106 - 23 = 221.0; at March 31, 2026 = 138.0 + 15.4 - 0 = 153.4 (Q1 2025 printed as nil). Cover: 647.8 / 138.0 = 4.69; 658.0 / 153.4 = 4.29; 724.8 / 221.0 = 3.28; 273 / 106 = 2.58. 6. Pro forma borrowings at July 1, 2026 = 6,111 + incremental term loan 3,000 = 9,111. The 3,000 of notes released from escrow are already inside 6,111. Contractual coupon run-rate on June 30, 2026 borrowings at printed rates = 850 x 5.64% + 2,250 x 6.75% + 1,500 x 6.500% + 1,500 x 6.875% + 11 x 4.70% = 47.9 + 151.9 + 97.5 + 103.1 + 0.5 = 401.0 (rounded components sum to 400.9), before the incremental term loan whose margin is not supplied. Floating-rate borrowings (term loan 850 and ABL 11) are 14.1% of 6,111 at June 30, 2026; including the 3,000 incremental term loan (assumed floating, as it is Term SOFR based) they are 3,861 of 9,111, or 42.4%, so a 100 basis point rise adds about 38.6 of annual interest. 7. Liquidity = cash + ABL availability: 2,361.6 + 1,970 = 4,331.6; 3,046.3 + 1,980 = 5,026.3; 2,774 + 1,930 = 4,704, agreeing with the filing's 4.70 billion. Netting test for the ABL: commitment 2,000 less drawn 11 less letters of credit 62 = 1,927, which rounds to the stated 1.93 billion; at March 31, 2026, 2,000 less 21.2 = 1,978.8 rounds to 1.98 billion. Both fit capacity stated net of letters of credit. At December 31, 2025, 2,000 less 21.2 = 1,978.8 does not equal the stated 1.97 billion, which implies a borrowing base below commitments at that date. If the stated June 2026 figure were instead before letters of credit, liquidity would be 4,642. 8. Covenant trigger: 10% of the lesser of the borrowing base and commitments of 2,000 is at most 200, so the trigger is the greater of 120 and at most 200, that is at most 200. Availability of 1,930 is at least 9.65 times the trigger (1,930 / 200 = 9.65); the agreement's own availability definition is not supplied, so the stated borrowing capacity is used as a proxy. 9. EBITDA before management add-backs = net loss + taxes + net interest + depreciation + amortisation. FY2025: -279.4 - 57.7 + 47.7 + 108.4 + 314.7 = 133.7. Q1 2026: -227.1 - 53.2 + 31.1 + 47.3 + 116.9 = -85.0. Q2 2026: -55 - 22 + 38 + 58 + 140 = 159. H1 2026: -282 - 75 + 69 + 105 + 257 = 74. H1 2025: -50 - 169 - 26 + 27 + 80 = -138. LTM = 133.7 + 74 - (-138) = 345.7. Add-backs LTM = 724.8 - 345.7 = 379.1. 10. LTM add-back detail = FY2025 + H1 2026 - H1 2025: stock compensation 144.5 + 68 - 85 = 127.5; restructuring 59.6 + 24 - 35 = 48.6; transaction 83.7 + 71 - 76 = 78.7; transformation 44.9 + 36 - 12 = 68.9; inventory fair value 131.7 + 0 - 80 = 51.7; loss on debt extinguishment 49.7 + 0 - 46 = 3.7; total 379.1 (127.5 + 48.6 + 78.7 + 68.9 + 51.7 + 3.7). Leverage on EBITDA before add-backs: 6,111 / 345.7 = 17.68; net 3,337 / 345.7 = 9.65. 11. Other LTM flows: net sales 6,842.2 + 4,976 - 1,920 = 9,898.2; gross profit 1,572.7 + 1,212 - 407 = 2,377.7; net loss -279.4 - 282 + 50 = -511.4; cash from operations 261.4 - 146 + 138 = 253.4; capex 78.2 + 54 - 20 = 112.2; cash taxes 38.2 + 5 - 35 = 8.2; preferred dividends 104.8 (90.0 + 14.8) + 84 (45 + 16 + 23) - 45 = 143.8. Adjusted EBITDA margin LTM 724.8 / 9,898.2 = 7.3%. 12. Quarterly derivations: Q2 2026 = H1 2026 less Q1 2026. Cash from operations -146 - 70.6 = -216.6; capex 54 - 22.5 = 31.5; cash interest 106 - 15.4 = 90.6; cash taxes 5 - 1.4 = 3.6; preferred dividends 84 - 30.4 = 53.6 (Q1 2026: 22.5 + 7.9 = 30.4). Cash from operations less capex: FY2025 261.4 - 78.2 = 183.2; Q1 48.1; Q2 -248.1; H1 -200; LTM 253.4 - 112.2 = 141.2. 13. Lease liabilities: finance December 2025 49.2 + 138.7 = 187.9; March 2026 49.8 + 129.6 = 179.4; June 2026 53 + 130 = 183. Operating December 2025 107.5 + 561.8 = 669.3; March 2026 110.1 + 554.4 = 664.5; June 2026 136 + 678 = 814. 14. TopBuild funding check: cash consideration of approximately 6.4 billion versus sources named in the filing of 3,000 (notes) + 3,000 (incremental term loan) + 1,000 (Series C) = 7,000. The excess of about 600 covers fees and expenses or remains as cash; the filing does not split it, so post-closing cash is Not calculable. 15. Maturity totals: 0 + 0 + 0 + 0 + 11 + 1,500 + 3,100 + 3,000 + 1,500 = 9,111 = 6,111 + 3,000.

facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: The credit story is an acquisition-led roll-up. QXO changed from a small software business into a roofing distributor on April 29, 2025 by buying Beacon, added Kodiak (lumber, trusses, windows and doors, construction supplies) on April 1, 2026, and agreed on April 18, 2026 to buy TopBuild (insulation distribution and installation), which closed on July 1, 2026, after the latest balance sheet date. The operating business is a branch-based distributor with a diversified customer base, no customer above 1% of sales, concentrated suppliers, strong seasonality and results driven by repair and re-roofing demand that management describes as largely non-discretionary. Each deal was paid for with a different mix: Kodiak with preferred stock and shares while its own debt was repaid, TopBuild with new debt, preferred stock and shares. Debt sits at the operating subsidiary; preferred stock, which carries senior-to-common cash dividends and a cash redemption right on a fundamental change for the Series C holders, sits at the parent. For a creditor the questions are integration execution on three businesses at once, how much of the added earnings reach the borrower's cash flow, and how control rights and preferred claims are used. The sources describe actions to date but not the executed covenant packages or any related-party arrangements, so governance conclusions are bounded.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: Beacon (closed April 29, 2025). Under a merger agreement dated March 20, 2025, QXO acquired Beacon for a net purchase price that the June 2026 quarterly report gives as 10.64 billion (10-Q Q2 2026, page:53). Financing signed on April 29, 2025 comprised a 2.25 billion term loan, 2.25 billion of 6.75% senior secured notes due 2032 and an asset-based revolver of up to 2.0 billion, alongside equity raised in 2024 and 2025; the pages read do not give a full sources and uses table. A voluntary 1.40 billion term loan prepayment followed on May 29, 2025, and the quarterly report states that the equity proceeds of May 2025 were used to repay term loan debt (10-Q Q2 2026, page:21 and page:48). The term loan margin was reduced in November 2025. Beacon is treated as the predecessor for financial reporting (10-K, page:67).

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: Kodiak (closed April 1, 2026). QXO agreed on February 10, 2026 to buy Kodiak from Court Square Capital Partners and closed on April 1, 2026 for a net purchase price of 2.22 billion according to the quarterly report; the annual report's earlier figure was approximately 2.25 billion and the share count is stated as 13.2 million and 13.3 million in different places (logged in conflicts below, not reconciled). Consideration was cash of 478 to sellers, 1,503 to settle Kodiak's secured term loan and asset-based facility including accrued interest, and 257 of QXO shares. Series C proceeds funded a portion of the cash: 200,000 shares of Series C Preferred Stock were issued for 2.0 billion gross proceeds to funds managed by affiliates of Apollo Global Management, Inc. Kodiak added net sales of 595 and net income of 15 in the second quarter of 2026. Status: complete, with purchase accounting preliminary.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: TopBuild (closed July 1, 2026, a subsequent event for the June 30, 2026 balance sheet). The merger agreement dated April 18, 2026 values the deal at approximately 15 billion in cash and stock. About 91.0% of TopBuild holders elected cash, and after proration each TopBuild share received about 249.67 in cash and 10.212 QXO shares; QXO issued about 312.0 million shares and paid about 6.4 billion in cash. Use of proceeds named in the filing: 3.0 billion of senior notes (6.500% due July 15, 2031 and 6.875% due July 15, 2034) sold on June 17, 2026 into a segregated escrow and released on closing; a 3.0 billion incremental term loan under the existing term loan agreement maturing July 1, 2033; and 1.0 billion from the remaining 100,000 shares of Series C Preferred Stock, which exhausted the 3.0 billion Series C commitment. The filing says the initial accounting is incomplete and that preliminary purchase price allocation is expected in the quarterly report for the period ending September 30, 2026. It does not say whether TopBuild's own debt was assumed or repaid, what cash TopBuild brought, or the cash left after closing; these are Insufficient Information and matter directly for liquidity and leverage.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: New debt issues, summarised for the creditor. The 2031 and 2034 notes are guaranteed by the subsidiaries that guarantee the term loan and the 2032 notes and are unsecured after the escrow release, so they rank behind the secured term loan, secured notes and asset-based revolver on the collateral; each carries a 101% put on specified change of control and, for these two series, ratings events. The incremental term loan is floating rate with a margin not stated in the pages read, 1% annual amortisation and a 1.00% repricing premium for six months. Preferred stock raised alongside the debt adds senior-to-common claims at the parent. Quantities are in the financial base handoff. Liquidity effect: the 3,000 of escrow cash was excluded from liquidity of 4,704 at June 30, 2026 and was spent on closing, so the post-closing liquidity position is Not supplied.

facts.text: 1. Acquisition-led growth. Evidence: three acquisitions in about fourteen months and 6,111 of borrowings at June 30, 2026 before a further 3,000 incremental term loan (from the financial base). Risk mechanic: earnings from Kodiak and TopBuild must replace the cash flow burdened by new interest, preferred dividends and integration and transaction costs; first-half 2026 operating cash flow was negative and trailing Adjusted EBITDA excludes TopBuild. Credit implication: leverage tolerance and debt service depend on integration delivery that is not yet visible in reported figures; monitoring posture should treat the third-quarter 2026 report as the next decisive evidence. Countering evidence: liquidity of 4,704 before closing and no scheduled principal on the June 30, 2026 debt before 2030. 2. Revenue durability. Evidence: no customer above 1% of sales, repair and re-roofing share described by management as non-discretionary, 97% U.S. sales. Mechanic: demand tied to weather and the housing stock, but first-quarter earnings are near nil, so cash timing is seasonal. Implication: revenue is durable at the customer level; working capital and liquidity must carry the first quarter. Countering: supplier concentration of nearly 35% in three suppliers and vendor rebate dependence. 3. Margin and cash flow. Evidence: product cost increases outpaced selling price increases in 2026, and the company adds back large restructuring, transaction and transformation costs (financial base). Mechanic: incomplete pass-through of product costs compresses gross margin. Implication: cash conversion and the quality of Adjusted EBITDA are the key uncertainties, not top-line growth. 4. Claims ahead of and beside debt. Evidence: Series C holders can require cash redemption at the greater of stated value plus accrued dividends and as-converted value on a fundamental change, alongside the 101% put on the notes. Mechanic: a change of control triggers both a debt put and a preferred cash call on the same event. Implication: the preferred cash call and the notes put arise from the same event and the amounts are not netted in any source; the Series C stated value of 3,000 compares with liquidity of 4,704 before closing (see Calculations). This is a mechanic, not a recovery view. 5. Control and alignment. Evidence: voting concentration and board designation rights. Mechanic: control rights can influence capital allocation and approval of extraordinary transactions. Implication: willingness cannot be inferred from ownership identity; the documented behaviour to date is equity-funded growth and no common dividends, which is supportive, but the absence of executed covenant documents leaves capacity unassessed. Countering: none logged.

facts.label: Calculations
facts.text: 1. Funding of TopBuild named sources = 3,000 notes + 3,000 incremental term loan + 1,000 Series C = 7,000, of which new debt = 6,000. Debt share of the approximately 15,000 headline price = 6,000 / 15,000 = 40%. Cash consideration approximately 6,400 versus 7,000 raised leaves about 600 for fees and expenses or cash; the filing does not split it. 2. Kodiak consideration: 478 + 1,503 + 257 = 2,238 preliminary aggregate consideration, less cash acquired 16 = 2,222 (agrees to 10-Q Q2 2026, page:22). Series C gross proceeds 2,000 / 2,238 = 89.4%; shares 257 / 2,238 = 11.5%; the sum is 100.9%, so the filing's funding description is approximate against consideration and no reconciliation is attempted. 3. Kodiak share of second-quarter 2026 net sales = 595 / 3,246 = 18.3%; of complementary building products sales = 595 / 1,229 = 48.4%. 4. Preferred dividend run-rate after the July 1, 2026 Series C issuance, at printed rates on liquidation preference: Series C 3,000 x 4.75% = 142.5; Convertible Preferred 1,000 x 9% = 90.0; Mandatory Convertible Preferred 575 x 5.50% = 31.6 (575 = 11.5 million depositary shares x 1/20 x 1,000); total 264.1. First-half 2026 preferred dividends paid were 84 (45 + 16 + 23), and trailing twelve-month preferred dividends paid were 143.8 (CP-1). Series C dividends may be paid in shares at the company's discretion, so this is a ceiling on cash. 5. Series C redemption exposure on a fundamental change: stated value 3,000 (300,000 shares x 10,000) plus accrued dividends, or as-converted value if greater; 3,000 compares with liquidity of 4,704 at June 30, 2026 before the July 1 closing (CP-1); cash after closing is not reported, and the as-converted value depends on a share price that is not supplied. 6. Capital intensity: first-half 2026 capital expenditures 54 / net sales 4,976 = 1.1%. 7. Control: the 22.1% and 39.4% percentages are as of the 10-K and are not updated for roughly 312.0 million shares issued on July 1, 2026; no recalculation is possible from the pack.

rows.label: QXO is a roofing and building products distributor assembled through three acquisitions in about fourteen months, financed by a mix of equity, preferred stock and secured and unsecured debt. Ownership is concentrated and a very large integration is under way.
Management says demand is largely repair-driven; customers are diversified, but three suppliers account for nearly 35% of purchases and the first quarter is seasonally weak.
The TopBuild purchase was funded with 6,000 of new debt, 1,000 of preferred stock and about 312.0 million shares.
Preferred stock ranks ahead of common and Series C holders can require cash redemption on a fundamental change.
The chairman controls about 22.1% of votes and the board designation right of 40% sits with his investor group.

facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: QXO, Inc. is a liquid but heavily acquisitive credit whose leverage cannot yet be measured on the enlarged group, so the fundamental view is cautious and conditional on integration. The strongest support is liquidity of USD 4,704 million at June 30, 2026, no scheduled principal on that debt before 2030 and a customer base with no customer above 1% of sales. The weakest point is that borrowings of USD 6,111 million, rising to USD 9,111 million after the July 1, 2026 term loan, are measured against last-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA of USD 724.8 million that excludes TopBuild, 52.3% of which comes from add-backs. What decides the outcome is whether TopBuild and Kodiak earnings arrive and whether the add-backs fade. [CP-1, CP-1A]

facts.label: Credit assessment and thesis
facts.text: Thesis (Analyst Interpretation): QXO, Inc. has funded a roll-up of three businesses with a mix of preferred equity, shares and USD 9,111 million of borrowings, and its credit quality is set by whether the enlarged group converts that scale into cash earnings that comfortably exceed its interest and preferred dividend burden. [CP-1, CP-1A]

citations.quote: Thesis (Analyst Interpretation): QXO, Inc. has funded a roll-up of three businesses with a mix of preferred equity, shares and USD 9,111 million of borrowings, and its credit quality is set by whether the enlarged group converts that scale into cash earnings that comfortably exceed its interest and preferred dividend burden. [CP-1, CP-1A]

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: 1. Borrowings have nearly doubled and the earnings base has not caught up (Documentary Fact for the amounts, Analyst Interpretation for the reading). QXO, Inc.'s borrowings were USD 3,100.0 million at December 31, 2025 and March 31, 2026, USD 6,111 million at June 30, 2026 after USD 3,000 million of notes were sold into escrow for TopBuild, and USD 9,111 million after the USD 3,000 million incremental term loan on July 1, 2026. Reported gross leverage at June 30, 2026 was 8.43x and net leverage 4.60x, but the earnings measure of USD 724.8 million has no TopBuild contribution and only three months of Kodiak, while the debt includes the TopBuild financing. The mechanism is a timing mismatch between debt and earnings; the implication is that these ratios are not a steady-state reading and the third-quarter 2026 report is the next decisive evidence. [CP-1, CP-1A] 2. Adjusted EBITDA relies on large add-backs (Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation on recurrence). Of USD 724.8 million of last-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA, USD 379.1 million (52.3%) is add-backs, including USD 127.5 million of stock compensation, USD 78.7 million of transaction costs, USD 68.9 million of transformation costs, USD 51.7 million of inventory fair value and USD 48.6 million of restructuring. EBITDA before the add-backs is USD 345.7 million, which gives gross leverage of 17.68x and net leverage of 9.65x at June 30, 2026. Restructuring, transaction and transformation items appear in each period reported, so QXO, Inc. may keep incurring them while it integrates three businesses; if they recur, leverage tolerance is weaker than the adjusted figures imply. [CP-1] 3. Interest cover is flattered by the timing of coupons (Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation). Last-twelve-month cash interest was USD 221.0 million, giving cover of 3.28x, and cover was 2.58x in the six months to June 30, 2026. The coupons on the June 30, 2026 borrowings at printed rates are USD 401.0 million a year, so cover on that run-rate is about 1.81x before the incremental term loan, whose margin is not supplied, and before any TopBuild earnings. If the incremental loan were priced like the existing term loan, run-rate interest would be about USD 570.2 million and cover about 1.27x on earnings excluding TopBuild. This is an illustrative floor, not an estimate: it shows how much of the credit depends on TopBuild earnings. [CP-1] 4. Cash conversion is thin in the first half and after preferred dividends (Documentary Fact). Cash from operations was negative USD 146 million in the first half of 2026 as receivables and inventory built, and LTM cash from operations less capital expenditures was USD 141.2 million against preferred dividends paid of USD 143.8 million, leaving USD -2.6 million. The first quarter is seasonally weak and the company reports a net loss of USD 511.4 million over the period. [CP-1, CP-1A] 5. Liquidity and maturities are the main support (Documentary Fact). Liquidity was USD 4,704 million at June 30, 2026 (cash USD 2,774 million plus asset-based revolver availability USD 1,930 million), excluding USD 3,000 million of escrowed proceeds that funded the TopBuild closing. No scheduled principal on the June 30, 2026 borrowings falls due before the revolver's 2030 maturity (USD 11 million drawn); the maturities are USD 1,500 million in 2031, USD 3,100 million in 2032, USD 3,000 million in 2033 (the incremental loan) and USD 1,500 million in 2034. The springing fixed charge test on the revolver is not live, as availability of USD 1,930 million compares with a trigger of at most USD 200 million. The implication is low refinancing risk through 2030, but post-closing cash is Not supplied. [CP-1] 6. Rate exposure and claims ahead of or beside the debt are rising (Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation). Floating-rate borrowings are 14.1% of June 30, 2026 borrowings and 42.4% including the incremental term loan, so 100 basis points adds about USD 38.6 million of annual interest. The USD 3,000 million of 2031 and 2034 notes are unsecured behind the secured revolver, term loans and 2032 notes, and the group has senior-to-common preferred stock whose dividends could reach USD 264.1 million a year. Series C holders can require cash redemption on a fundamental change, an event that also triggers a 101% put on the notes, and the amounts are not netted in any source. [CP-1, CP-1A] 7. Governance is documented but not fully assessable (Documentary Fact; Insufficient Information). Documented actions to date are a Kodiak purchase funded with preferred stock and shares, no common dividends and preferred dividends paid in cash, with an option to pay Series C dividends in shares. Voting power is concentrated in the chairman at about 22.1% and a 40% board designation right sits with his investor group, as of the annual report. Related-party arrangements, executed covenant definitions and current ownership percentages after the TopBuild share issuance are Not supplied. [CP-1A]

facts.label: Calculations
facts.text: 1. Add-back share = add-backs 379.1 / LTM Adjusted EBITDA 724.8 = 52.3%. EBITDA before add-backs 345.7 / 724.8 = 47.7%. Leverage on EBITDA before add-backs: 6,111 / 345.7 = 17.68x gross and 3,337 / 345.7 = 9.65x net (CP-1 calculation 10). 2. EBITDA less capital expenditures = 724.8 - 112.2 = 612.6; over LTM cash interest 221.0 = 2.77x. 3. Cash from operations less capital expenditures, less preferred dividends paid: 141.2 - 143.8 = -2.6. 4. Fixed-rate share = (1,500 + 2,250 + 1,500) / 6,111 = 5,250 / 6,111 = 85.9%; floating 14.1%. After the incremental term loan, floating = (850 + 11 + 3,000) / 9,111 = 3,861 / 9,111 = 42.4%; fixed 5,250 / 9,111 = 57.6%. A 100 basis point rise on 3,861 = 38.6. The incremental loan is assumed floating because the filing states Term SOFR or base rate pricing. 5. Run-rate coupon on June 30, 2026 borrowings = 850 x 5.64% + 2,250 x 6.75% + 1,500 x 6.500% + 1,500 x 6.875% + 11 x 4.70% = 401.0 (CP-1 calculation 6). Cover on that run-rate = 724.8 / 401.0 = 1.81x. Illustrative: incremental term loan priced at the existing term loan rate of 5.64% (an assumption; the filing does not state the margin) = 3,000 x 5.64% = 169.2; run-rate 401.0 + 169.2 = 570.2; cover 724.8 / 570.2 = 1.27x. Both exclude interest income, commitment fees and any TopBuild earnings. 6. Illustrative earnings needed, not a covenant or target: gross leverage of 6.0x on 9,111 needs EBITDA of 1,518.5, which is 793.7 above 724.8; 5.0x needs 1,822.2, which is 1,097.4 above 724.8. 7. Secured share of borrowings after closing, assuming the incremental term loan carries the term loan's security (the filing says it is incurred under the same credit agreement): revolver 11 + term loan 850 + incremental 3,000 + 2032 notes 2,250 = 6,111, of 9,111 = 67.1%; unsecured notes 3,000 / 9,111 = 32.9%. 8. Preferred dividend ceiling 264.1 and Series C stated value 3,000 are from CP-1A calculations 4 and 5.

rows.label: QXO has ample liquidity but heavy, acquisition-driven borrowings that cannot yet be measured against the earnings of the enlarged group. The view is cautious and depends on TopBuild and Kodiak delivering earnings and on add-backs fading.
Borrowings rose from USD 3,100.0 million to USD 6,111 million at June 30, 2026 and to USD 9,111 million after the July 1, 2026 term loan.
Add-backs of USD 379.1 million make up 52.3% of last-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA of USD 724.8 million.
Cash interest cover was 3.28x, but coupons on the June 30, 2026 debt alone are USD 401.0 million a year.
Liquidity was USD 4,704 million at June 30, 2026 and no scheduled principal falls due before 2030.
Preferred stock could draw up to USD 264.1 million of dividends a year and Series C holders can demand cash on a change of control.
TopBuild and Kodiak earnings fall short of the debt and preferred claims taken on
Cash call on a change of control
Rate exposure on the incremental term loan

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| The filings and releases support the minimum credit snapshot for the QXO, Inc. consolidated group through the June 2026 quarter, with stated limitations. The TopBuild acquisition closed after quarter end and its effects are only partly reported. | Medium | No post-closing balance sheet, TopBuild financials or acquisition accounting is supplied, and the debt agreements are not in the pack. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Quarterly statements, debt note, lease note and liquidity inputs are present for the latest quarter and the prior year-end. | Net debt, liquidity and coverage can be built from filed figures for the June 2026 balance sheet. | High |
| The company closed a large acquisition on July 1, 2026 and its accounting is incomplete. | Debt, preferred stock and earnings after the quarter are not yet on a reported balance sheet. | Medium |
| Beacon is the predecessor and QXO history before April 29, 2025 is a different business. | Year-on-year comparisons and trailing figures need explicit perimeter labels. | Medium |

| Indentures, credit agreements and predecessor financial information are listed as exhibits but not supplied. | Debt terms can only be taken from the filed notes, not from executed documents. | Medium |
### Readiness view

The effective source set is adequate to start the requested minimum work, with bounded limitations: READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS for CP-1, CP-1A, CP-2 and CP-5. The set holds one audited annual report, three interim reports and three earnings releases, all issued by QXO, Inc. and all text-searchable. No consumer is CONDITIONAL or BLOCKED on source grounds. The main limits are the post-quarter TopBuild closing (reported only in narrative and notes), the absence of executed debt documents, and the absence of any investor presentation. This is a statement of source sufficiency only; it does not evaluate any downstream input contract or assert normalised quarters.
### Source profile by document
Document family, authority and perimeter come from located content, not file names.

- **10-K, FY2025.** Filed annual report for QXO, Inc. Cover: `10-K_2025-12-31_qxo-20251231.htm.jsonl` page:1: "FORM 10-K" and "For the fiscal year ended: December 31, 2025". Audited: page:60: "We have audited the accompanying consolidated balance sheet of QXO, Inc." Controlling filed authority for FY2025 statements, debt, leases and equity notes. The index on page:59 lists two audit reports (PCAOB IDs 34 and 688); the second report opens on page:62 with "as of December 31, 2024", so the prior-year balance sheet and year were audited by a different firm from the FY2025 auditor. The 10-K therefore carries two auditors across the two years. FY2025 contains Beacon only from the acquisition date: `EX-99.1_2026-02-25_qxoq4-25earningsrelease.htm.jsonl` page:1: "include the legacy Beacon Roofing Supply, Inc. (“Beacon”) operational results from the date of acquisition on April 29, 2025".

- **10-Q, Q3 2025.** Interim, unaudited, supports quarter, nine-month and balance sheet at September 30, 2025, and the Beacon measurement-period goodwill adjustment (page:19). It is the only source for Q3 2025 discrete figures, which are needed for any trailing view together with the 10-K.

- **10-Q, Q1 2026.** Interim, unaudited, quarter ended March 31, 2026. Reports whole amounts with one decimal (goodwill table, page:10), whereas the June 2026 report changed rounding, see conflicts below.

- **10-Q, Q2 2026.** Latest interim filing, signed August 14, 2026 (page:99). Holds the debt note (page:44 to page:51), leases (page:51), equity and mezzanine equity (page:30 onward), acquisitions (page:18 to page:26) and MD&A (page:52 onward). Perimeter is QXO, Inc. and subsidiaries; debt sits at the subsidiary QXO Building Products, Inc. and the notes were issued by the Issuer, which assumed the Beacon financing: `10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl` page:45: "QXO Building Products assumed the obligations under the 2032 Notes and the 2032 Indenture". The term loan and ABL borrower is the subsidiary with Queen HoldCo, LLC as Holdings (page:47). Whether the parent QXO, Inc. itself is a guarantor of the notes is not stated in the pages read and is a gap.

- **Earnings releases (three).** Management documents furnished as Exhibit 99.1. They provide attributed non-GAAP measures (Adjusted EBITDA, Adjusted Net Income) with reconciliations and quarter versus year-to-date columns. They do not override the filings. The August release (`EX-99.1_2026-08-13_qxoq2-26earningsrelease.htm.jsonl` page:1) shows three-month and six-month columns, so quarter and year-to-date figures are separately available for June 2026.
### Coverage by evidence need

- **Statements and periods.** Balance sheet, operations and cash flow for the six months to June 30, 2026 are in the August release (page:7 to page:9) and the Q2 10-Q. Discrete quarters can be located: Q2 2026 (August release page:1), Q1 2026 (May release page:1), Q4 2025 (February release page:1), Q3 2025 (10-Q September 2025). Quarter and year-to-date distinctions are labelled in each release.

- **Debt.** The Q2 10-Q debt table lists each instrument with principal, carrying value and fair value: `10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl` page:44: "Term Loan Facility(2) $ 850 $ 829 $ 848" and "2032 Senior Secured Notes(4) 2,250 2,232 2,326". Rates, maturities, security and redemption terms are described in the note (page:45 to page:51).

- **Liquidity.** ABL capacity and letters of credit are printed: page:49: "the Borrower had $1.93 billion borrowing capacity under the ABL Facility" and page:51: "the Borrower and its restricted subsidiaries had $62 million in outstanding standby letters of credit issued under the ABL Facility". Whether the stated capacity is before or after the letters of credit is not stated in the passage; this is for the downstream liquidity step to resolve and flag.

- **Covenants.** Only one maintenance test is described, a springing test: page:50: "maintain a minimum fixed charge coverage ratio of 1.0 to 1.0 at any time that availability is less than". Compliance is stated for the indentures, term loan and ABL (page:46, page:48, page:50). Defined terms are not supplied, so a covenant-basis ratio cannot be rebuilt.
- **Cash interest and taxes.** Printed in the August release cash flow supplement (page:9): "Interest $ 106 $ 23" and "Income taxes, net of refunds $ 5 $ 35" for six months 2026 and 2025.
- **Leases.** Maturity table of operating and finance leases at June 30, 2026 is printed (page:51).

- **Preferred and mezzanine equity.** Series C Preferred Stock is mezzanine equity (page:36); Convertible and Mandatory Convertible Preferred are in equity with dividends in the cash flow statement (August release page:8 to page:9).

- **Segments and KPIs.** Net sales by line of business are in the August release (page:9). The Q2 10-Q states one operating segment (page:28: "views its operations and manages its business as a single operating segment") and plans new reportable segments after Kodiak and TopBuild (page:29: "plans to report financial information based on its new reportable segments in the future"). No segment profit measure exists in the pack; this is a limitation for CP-1.

- **Business and transaction narrative.** Beacon, Kodiak and TopBuild transactions, with funding, are described in the Q2 10-Q (page:53 to page:54): "The Company completed its acquisition of TopBuild for a purchase price of approximately $15 billion."
### Strongest contrary evidence and limitations

- **Subsequent event is incomplete.** The TopBuild closing date is after the balance sheet date, and the filing says: page:26: "initial accounting for the business combination is incomplete and the Company is not yet able to disclose the provisional amounts". Mechanism: the June 30 balance sheet shows escrowed proceeds as restricted cash, page:8 of the August release footnote: "restricted cash of $3.0 billion, representing the gross proceeds from the issuance of the 6.500% Senior Notes due 2031 and 6.875% Senior Notes due 2034". Debt, preferred stock, shares and earnings capacity after July 1, 2026 therefore sit outside the reported balance sheet. Consequence: any leverage or liquidity measure built on June 30, 2026 figures mixes a pre-closing balance sheet with a financing that closed on July 1, 2026, and downstream modules must show a pro forma debt bridge from narrative only and label it as constructed.

- **Perimeter changes.** QXO was a software and services company before Beacon: `10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl` page:18: "the financial results of QXO as of and for any periods prior to April 29, 2025 do not include the financial results of Beacon". Beacon was determined the predecessor (page:12). The pack carries no complete Beacon predecessor statements: page:98: "The predecessor financial information is included as Exhibit 99.1 to this Quarterly Report and is incorporated herein by reference" and the exhibit index (page:99) shows it as a prior filing, not in the pack. Consequence: FY2025 and first-half 2025 comparatives are not like-for-like with 2026, and Kodiak contributes only from April 1, 2026 (August release page:1: "from the date of acquisition on April 1, 2026"). Trailing twelve-month figures would blend four different perimeters.

- **Mid-year presentation change.** `10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl` page:12 records that rounding changed in the second quarter of 2026 to the nearest whole million, while earlier filings and the February and May releases show one decimal. Conflict locators: May release page:1 "$ 1,730.2" versus August release page:1 "$ 4,976". Consequence: sums across periods can differ by rounding; this is a presentation difference, not a restatement, and no restatement was found by a search for restatement language beyond the cover check box.

- **Executed documents absent.** The exhibit list shows the indentures, supplemental indentures and the incremental term loan amendment as filed exhibits (`10-Q_2026-06-30_qxo-20260630.htm.jsonl` page:98 and page:99) but none is in the pack. Consequence: covenant definitions, baskets, restricted payment tests, guarantor lists and change-of-control terms are known only through the note summaries. The filing says restrictions are not significant for common dividends (page:51), which is a management statement.

- **No presentation or Q3 2026 results.** No investor deck and no results for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 are in the pack, and the Q2 10-Q says the preliminary TopBuild purchase price allocation is expected in the September 2026 quarter report. Whether that report was available before the cutoff is not evidenced by the pack; nothing after the cutoff is assumed.

- **Management claims.** Market-position and target statements (for example the "$50 billion in annual revenue within the decade" target) are management assertions in the releases (August release page:2), not filed fact; non-GAAP measures carry management add-backs (restructuring, transaction, transformation, stock-based compensation) that need reconciliation to filed figures downstream.
### Consumer assessment
| Consumer | Status | Basis and limitations carried forward |

| CP-1 (financial extraction, quarters and debt) | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Statements, debt table, lease table, cash interest and tax are located. Seasonality is strong: the first quarter earns almost nothing and the half-year cash flow from operations is negative. ## Calculations

All inputs are as printed; US$ millions unless stated. Rounding differs by source: Q2 2026 and half-year figures are whole millions, FY2025 and Q1 2026 have one decimal, so results are accurate to roughly 1.

1. LTM Adjusted EBITDA at June 30, 2026 = FY2025 647.8 + H1 2026 273 - H1 2025 196 = 724.8. LTM at March 31, 2026 = 647.8 + 1.2 - (-9.0) = 658.0. Check on H1 2025: Q1 2025 (-9.0) plus Q2 2025 (204) = 195 against 196 printed, a rounding difference.
2. Borrowings principal at June 30, 2026 = long-term debt principal 6,100 (850 + 1,500 + 2,250 + 1,500) + ABL 11 = 6,111. At December 31, 2025 and March 31, 2026 = 850.0 + 2,250.0 = 3,100.0.

3. Net debt = principal less unrestricted cash: December 2025 3,100.0 - 2,361.6 = 738.4; March 2026 3,100.0 - 3,046.3 = 53.7; June 2026 6,111 - 2,774 = 3,337. If the 3,000 escrow were treated as cash, June net debt would be 337, but that cash was committed to the purchase and released July 1, 2026.

6. Pro forma borrowings at July 1, 2026 = 6,111 + incremental term loan 3,000 = 9,111. The 3,000 of notes released from escrow are already inside 6,111. Contractual coupon run-rate on June 30, 2026 borrowings at printed rates = 850 x 5.64% + 2,250 x 6.75% + 1,500 x 6.500% + 1,500 x 6.875% + 11 x 4.70% = 47.9 + 151.9 + 97.5 + 103.1 + 0.5 = 401.0 (rounded components sum to 400.9), before the incremental term loan whose margin is not supplied. Floating-rate borrowings (term loan 850 and ABL 11) are 14.1% of 6,111 at June 30, 2026; including the 3,000 incremental term loan (assumed floating, as it is Term SOFR based) they are 3,861 of 9,111, or 42.4%, so a 100 basis point rise adds about 38.6 of annual interest.

7. Liquidity = cash + ABL availability: 2,361.6 + 1,970 = 4,331.6; 3,046.3 + 1,980 = 5,026.3; 2,774 + 1,930 = 4,704, agreeing with the filing's 4.70 billion. Netting test for the ABL: commitment 2,000 less drawn 11 less letters of credit 62 = 1,927, which rounds to the stated 1.93 billion; at March 31, 2026, 2,000 less 21.2 = 1,978.8 rounds to 1.98 billion. Both fit capacity stated net of letters of credit. At December 31, 2025, 2,000 less 21.2 = 1,978.8 does not equal the stated 1.97 billion, which implies a borrowing base below commitments at that date. If the stated June 2026 figure were instead before letters of credit, liquidity would be 4,642.

8. Covenant trigger: 10% of the lesser of the borrowing base and commitments of 2,000 is at most 200, so the trigger is the greater of 120 and at most 200, that is at most 200. Availability of 1,930 is at least 9.65 times the trigger (1,930 / 200 = 9.65); the agreement's own availability definition is not supplied, so the stated borrowing capacity is used as a proxy.

10. Cash from operations -146 - 70.6 = -216.6; capex 54 - 22.5 = 31.5; cash interest 106 - 15.4 = 90.6; cash taxes 5 - 1.4 = 3.6; preferred dividends 84 - 30.4 = 53.6 (Q1 2026: 22.5 + 7.9 = 30.4). Cash from operations less capex: FY2025 261.4 - 78.2 = 183.2; Q1 48.1; Q2 -248.1; H1 -200; LTM 253.4 - 112.2 = 141.2.

14. TopBuild funding check: cash consideration of approximately 6.4 billion versus sources named in the filing of 3,000 (notes) + 3,000 (incremental term loan) + 1,000 (Series C) = 7,000. The excess of about 600 covers fees and expenses or remains as cash; the filing does not split it, so post-closing cash is Not calculable.

## Findings
### Reader summary

Ownership is concentrated and a very large integration is under way. | Medium | TopBuild accounting is incomplete, and executed documents and related-party disclosures are not in the pack. |

### Business and transaction view

The credit story is an acquisition-led roll-up. QXO changed from a small software business into a roofing distributor on April 29, 2025 by buying Beacon, added Kodiak (lumber, trusses, windows and doors, construction supplies) on April 1, 2026, and agreed on April 18, 2026 to buy TopBuild (insulation distribution and installation), which closed on July 1, 2026, after the latest balance sheet date. The operating business is a branch-based distributor with a diversified customer base, no customer above 1% of sales, concentrated suppliers, strong seasonality and results driven by repair and re-roofing demand that management describes as largely non-discretionary. Each deal was paid for with a different mix: Kodiak with preferred stock and shares while its own debt was repaid, TopBuild with new debt, preferred stock and shares. Debt sits at the operating subsidiary; preferred stock, which carries senior-to-common cash dividends and a cash redemption right on a fundamental change for the Series C holders, sits at the parent. For a creditor the questions are integration execution on three businesses at once, how much of the added earnings reach the borrower's cash flow, and how control rights and preferred claims are used. The sources describe actions to date but not the executed covenant packages or any related-party arrangements, so governance conclusions are bounded.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

Beacon (closed April 29, 2025). Under a merger agreement dated March 20, 2025, QXO acquired Beacon for a net purchase price that the June 2026 quarterly report gives as 10.64 billion (10-Q Q2 2026, page:53). Financing signed on April 29, 2025 comprised a 2.25 billion term loan, 2.25 billion of 6.75% senior secured notes due 2032 and an asset-based revolver of up to 2.0 billion, alongside equity raised in 2024 and 2025; the pages read do not give a full sources and uses table. A voluntary 1.40 billion term loan prepayment followed on May 29, 2025, and the quarterly report states that the equity proceeds of May 2025 were used to repay term loan debt (10-Q Q2 2026, page:21 and page:48). The term loan margin was reduced in November 2025. Beacon is treated as the predecessor for financial reporting (10-K, page:67).

Kodiak (closed April 1, 2026). QXO agreed on February 10, 2026 to buy Kodiak from Court Square Capital Partners and closed on April 1, 2026 for a net purchase price of 2.22 billion according to the quarterly report; the annual report's earlier figure was approximately 2.25 billion and the share count is stated as 13.2 million and 13.3 million in different places (logged in conflicts below, not reconciled). Consideration was cash of 478 to sellers, 1,503 to settle Kodiak's secured term loan and asset-based facility including accrued interest, and 257 of QXO shares. Series C proceeds funded a portion of the cash: 200,000 shares of Series C Preferred Stock were issued for 2.0 billion gross proceeds to funds managed by affiliates of Apollo Global Management, Inc. Kodiak added net sales of 595 and net income of 15 in the second quarter of 2026. Status: complete, with purchase accounting preliminary.

TopBuild (closed July 1, 2026, a subsequent event for the June 30, 2026 balance sheet). The merger agreement dated April 18, 2026 values the deal at approximately 15 billion in cash and stock. About 91.0% of TopBuild holders elected cash, and after proration each TopBuild share received about 249.67 in cash and 10.212 QXO shares; QXO issued about 312.0 million shares and paid about 6.4 billion in cash. Use of proceeds named in the filing: 3.0 billion of senior notes (6.500% due July 15, 2031 and 6.875% due July 15, 2034) sold on June 17, 2026 into a segregated escrow and released on closing; a 3.0 billion incremental term loan under the existing term loan agreement maturing July 1, 2033; and 1.0 billion from the remaining 100,000 shares of Series C Preferred Stock, which exhausted the 3.0 billion Series C commitment. The filing says the initial accounting is incomplete and that preliminary purchase price allocation is expected in the quarterly report for the period ending September 30, 2026. It does not say whether TopBuild's own debt was assumed or repaid, what cash TopBuild brought, or the cash left after closing; these are Insufficient Information and matter directly for liquidity and leverage.

New debt issues, summarised for the creditor. The 2031 and 2034 notes are guaranteed by the subsidiaries that guarantee the term loan and the 2032 notes and are unsecured after the escrow release, so they rank behind the secured term loan, secured notes and asset-based revolver on the collateral; each carries a 101% put on specified change of control and, for these two series, ratings events. The incremental term loan is floating rate with a margin not stated in the pages read, 1% annual amortisation and a 1.00% repricing premium for six months. Preferred stock raised alongside the debt adds senior-to-common claims at the parent. Quantities are in the financial base handoff. Liquidity effect: the 3,000 of escrow cash was excluded from liquidity of 4,704 at June 30, 2026 and was spent on closing, so the post-closing liquidity position is Not supplied.

### Credit translations

1. Acquisition-led growth. Evidence: three acquisitions in about fourteen months and 6,111 of borrowings at June 30, 2026 before a further 3,000 incremental term loan (from the financial base). Risk mechanic: earnings from Kodiak and TopBuild must replace the cash flow burdened by new interest, preferred dividends and integration and transaction costs; first-half 2026 operating cash flow was negative and trailing Adjusted EBITDA excludes TopBuild. Credit implication: leverage tolerance and debt service depend on integration delivery that is not yet visible in reported figures; monitoring posture should treat the third-quarter 2026 report as the next decisive evidence. Countering evidence: liquidity of 4,704 before closing and no scheduled principal on the June 30, 2026 debt before 2030.

2. Revenue durability. Evidence: no customer above 1% of sales, repair and re-roofing share described by management as non-discretionary, 97% U.S. sales. Mechanic: demand tied to weather and the housing stock, but first-quarter earnings are near nil, so cash timing is seasonal. Implication: revenue is durable at the customer level; working capital and liquidity must carry the first quarter. Countering: supplier concentration of nearly 35% in three suppliers and vendor rebate dependence.

3. Margin and cash flow. Evidence: product cost increases outpaced selling price increases in 2026, and the company adds back large restructuring, transaction and transformation costs (financial base). Mechanic: incomplete pass-through of product costs compresses gross margin. Implication: cash conversion and the quality of Adjusted EBITDA are the key uncertainties, not top-line growth.

4. Claims ahead of and beside debt. Evidence: Series C holders can require cash redemption at the greater of stated value plus accrued dividends and as-converted value on a fundamental change, alongside the 101% put on the notes. Mechanic: a change of control triggers both a debt put and a preferred cash call on the same event. Implication: the preferred cash call and the notes put arise from the same event and the amounts are not netted in any source; the Series C stated value of 3,000 compares with liquidity of 4,704 before closing (see Calculations). This is a mechanic, not a recovery view.

5. Control and alignment. Evidence: voting concentration and board designation rights. Mechanic: control rights can influence capital allocation and approval of extraordinary transactions. Implication: willingness cannot be inferred from ownership identity; the documented behaviour to date is equity-funded growth and no common dividends, which is supportive, but the absence of executed covenant documents leaves capacity unassessed. Countering: none logged.

## Calculations

1. Funding of TopBuild named sources = 3,000 notes + 3,000 incremental term loan + 1,000 Series C = 7,000, of which new debt = 6,000. Debt share of the approximately 15,000 headline price = 6,000 / 15,000 = 40%. Cash consideration approximately 6,400 versus 7,000 raised leaves about 600 for fees and expenses or cash; the filing does not split it.

2. Kodiak consideration: 478 + 1,503 + 257 = 2,238 preliminary aggregate consideration, less cash acquired 16 = 2,222 (agrees to 10-Q Q2 2026, page:22). Series C gross proceeds 2,000 / 2,238 = 89.4%; shares 257 / 2,238 = 11.5%; the sum is 100.9%, so the filing's funding description is approximate against consideration and no reconciliation is attempted.
3. Kodiak share of second-quarter 2026 net sales = 595 / 3,246 = 18.3%; of complementary building products sales = 595 / 1,229 = 48.4%.

4. Preferred dividend run-rate after the July 1, 2026 Series C issuance, at printed rates on liquidation preference: Series C 3,000 x 4.75% = 142.5; Convertible Preferred 1,000 x 9% = 90.0; Mandatory Convertible Preferred 575 x 5.50% = 31.6 (575 = 11.5 million depositary shares x 1/20 x 1,000); total 264.1. First-half 2026 preferred dividends paid were 84 (45 + 16 + 23), and trailing twelve-month preferred dividends paid were 143.8 (CP-1). Series C dividends may be paid in shares at the company's discretion, so this is a ceiling on cash.

5. Series C redemption exposure on a fundamental change: stated value 3,000 (300,000 shares x 10,000) plus accrued dividends, or as-converted value if greater; 3,000 compares with liquidity of 4,704 at June 30, 2026 before the July 1 closing (CP-1); cash after closing is not reported, and the as-converted value depends on a share price that is not supplied.
6. Capital intensity: first-half 2026 capital expenditures 54 / net sales 4,976 = 1.1%.

Fundamental credit synthesis for QXO, Inc., as of 2026-11-05, pathway credit_snapshot, reporting currency USD, built only from the financial base and the business and transaction context supplied by earlier modules. Scope is the QXO, Inc. group as reported to June 30, 2026 plus the events of July 1, 2026 that the June 2026 quarterly report discloses. No peer ranking, instrument recommendation or recovery conclusion is given.
## Sources
CP-2 reads upstream handoffs only and quotes no source text. The issuer sources behind those handoffs are listed with their exact names and sha256 values.

| EX-99.1_2026-05-12_qxoq1-26earningsrelease.htm.jsonl | cb6d12c2f11a6aae12e16b22f726607cf654ffc6f9c813c160df8563f9de9aa2 |
Run settings (not issuer evidence): context, sha256 6a7b1beefd6814e2c0ed169307a2fa7c8234de27933b1d6c6e62ef434dbf5add.
Supplied handoffs:
| Module | sha256 |
| CP-1 | 0c4570b0cb02f79e4f6bc512ceeaaaa35a45ba07e203d0adcef2870aec1b148f |
| CP-1A | c18abc5e3bcca0ebf51a2c43e611becd725c810db3ea10aa7a3e536b97687d36 |

Basis labels used below: [CP-1] is the financial base (its figures are US dollars in millions as printed there); [CP-1A] is the business and transaction context, including its Category tags and logged conflicts. All amounts in prose below are USD millions unless a ratio or percentage is shown.
## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| QXO has ample liquidity but heavy, acquisition-driven borrowings that cannot yet be measured against the earnings of the enlarged group. The view is cautious and depends on TopBuild and Kodiak delivering earnings and on add-backs fading. | Low | Post-closing earnings, cash and purchase accounting are not reported, and the adjusted earnings measure relies on large add-backs. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Borrowings rose from USD 3,100.0 million to USD 6,111 million at June 30, 2026 and to USD 9,111 million after the July 1, 2026 term loan. | Reported leverage of 8.43x gross and 4.60x net is measured on earnings that exclude TopBuild. | Medium |

| Add-backs of USD 379.1 million make up 52.3% of last-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA of USD 724.8 million. | Before add-backs, gross leverage is 17.68x; leverage tolerance depends on the add-backs falling away. | Medium |

| Cash interest cover was 3.28x, but coupons on the June 30, 2026 debt alone are USD 401.0 million a year. | Cover on current coupons is about 1.81x before the new term loan and before TopBuild earnings. | Medium |
| Liquidity was USD 4,704 million at June 30, 2026 and no scheduled principal falls due before 2030. | Near-term refinancing risk is low; post-closing cash is not reported. | Medium |

| Preferred stock could draw up to USD 264.1 million of dividends a year and Series C holders can demand cash on a change of control. | Preferred claims compete with debt service at the parent. | Medium |
### Credit view

QXO, Inc. is a liquid but heavily acquisitive credit whose leverage cannot yet be measured on the enlarged group, so the fundamental view is cautious and conditional on integration. The strongest support is liquidity of USD 4,704 million at June 30, 2026, no scheduled principal on that debt before 2030 and a customer base with no customer above 1% of sales. The weakest point is that borrowings of USD 6,111 million, rising to USD 9,111 million after the July 1, 2026 term loan, are measured against last-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA of USD 724.8 million that excludes TopBuild, 52.3% of which comes from add-backs. What decides the outcome is whether TopBuild and Kodiak earnings arrive and whether the add-backs fade. [CP-1, CP-1A]
### Credit assessment and thesis
| Assessment | View | Category | Confidence | Basis and limitation |

| Group as reported at June 30, 2026 | Liquid, with borrowings roughly double year-end and a thin earnings base relative to them | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | CP-1 balance sheet, ratios and liquidity; escrowed note proceeds are excluded from liquidity and were released on July 1, 2026 |

| Group after the TopBuild closing | Not measurable on reported figures; borrowings USD 9,111 million with no TopBuild earnings, cash or purchase accounting reported | Insufficient Information | Low | Missing: TopBuild earnings, balance sheet, debt assumed or repaid, cash after closing, incremental term loan margin; matters because every leverage, cover and liquidity ratio changes |

Thesis (Analyst Interpretation): QXO, Inc. has funded a roll-up of three businesses with a mix of preferred equity, shares and USD 9,111 million of borrowings, and its credit quality is set by whether the enlarged group converts that scale into cash earnings that comfortably exceed its interest and preferred dividend burden. [CP-1, CP-1A]
### Key findings

1. Borrowings have nearly doubled and the earnings base has not caught up (Documentary Fact for the amounts, Analyst Interpretation for the reading). QXO, Inc.'s borrowings were USD 3,100.0 million at December 31, 2025 and March 31, 2026, USD 6,111 million at June 30, 2026 after USD 3,000 million of notes were sold into escrow for TopBuild, and USD 9,111 million after the USD 3,000 million incremental term loan on July 1, 2026. Reported gross leverage at June 30, 2026 was 8.43x and net leverage 4.60x, but the earnings measure of USD 724.8 million has no TopBuild contribution and only three months of Kodiak, while the debt includes the TopBuild financing. The mechanism is a timing mismatch between debt and earnings; the implication is that these ratios are not a steady-state reading and the third-quarter 2026 report is the next decisive evidence. [CP-1, CP-1A]

2. Adjusted EBITDA relies on large add-backs (Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation on recurrence). Of USD 724.8 million of last-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA, USD 379.1 million (52.3%) is add-backs, including USD 127.5 million of stock compensation, USD 78.7 million of transaction costs, USD 68.9 million of transformation costs, USD 51.7 million of inventory fair value and USD 48.6 million of restructuring. EBITDA before the add-backs is USD 345.7 million, which gives gross leverage of 17.68x and net leverage of 9.65x at June 30, 2026. Restructuring, transaction and transformation items appear in each period reported, so QXO, Inc. may keep incurring them while it integrates three businesses; if they recur, leverage tolerance is weaker than the adjusted figures imply. [CP-1]

3. Interest cover is flattered by the timing of coupons (Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation). Last-twelve-month cash interest was USD 221.0 million, giving cover of 3.28x, and cover was 2.58x in the six months to June 30, 2026. The coupons on the June 30, 2026 borrowings at printed rates are USD 401.0 million a year, so cover on that run-rate is about 1.81x before the incremental term loan, whose margin is not supplied, and before any TopBuild earnings. If the incremental loan were priced like the existing term loan, run-rate interest would be about USD 570.2 million and cover about 1.27x on earnings excluding TopBuild. This is an illustrative floor, not an estimate: it shows how much of the credit depends on TopBuild earnings. [CP-1]

4. Cash conversion is thin in the first half and after preferred dividends (Documentary Fact). Cash from operations was negative USD 146 million in the first half of 2026 as receivables and inventory built, and LTM cash from operations less capital expenditures was USD 141.2 million against preferred dividends paid of USD 143.8 million, leaving USD -2.6 million. The first quarter is seasonally weak and the company reports a net loss of USD 511.4 million over the period. [CP-1, CP-1A]

5. Liquidity and maturities are the main support (Documentary Fact). Liquidity was USD 4,704 million at June 30, 2026 (cash USD 2,774 million plus asset-based revolver availability USD 1,930 million), excluding USD 3,000 million of escrowed proceeds that funded the TopBuild closing. No scheduled principal on the June 30, 2026 borrowings falls due before the revolver's 2030 maturity (USD 11 million drawn); the maturities are USD 1,500 million in 2031, USD 3,100 million in 2032, USD 3,000 million in 2033 (the incremental loan) and USD 1,500 million in 2034. The springing fixed charge test on the revolver is not live, as availability of USD 1,930 million compares with a trigger of at most USD 200 million. The implication is low refinancing risk through 2030, but post-closing cash is Not supplied. [CP-1]

6. Rate exposure and claims ahead of or beside the debt are rising (Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation). Floating-rate borrowings are 14.1% of June 30, 2026 borrowings and 42.4% including the incremental term loan, so 100 basis points adds about USD 38.6 million of annual interest. The USD 3,000 million of 2031 and 2034 notes are unsecured behind the secured revolver, term loans and 2032 notes, and the group has senior-to-common preferred stock whose dividends could reach USD 264.1 million a year. Series C holders can require cash redemption on a fundamental change, an event that also triggers a 101% put on the notes, and the amounts are not netted in any source. [CP-1, CP-1A]

7. Governance is documented but not fully assessable (Documentary Fact; Insufficient Information). Documented actions to date are a Kodiak purchase funded with preferred stock and shares, no common dividends and preferred dividends paid in cash, with an option to pay Series C dividends in shares. Voting power is concentrated in the chairman at about 22.1% and a 40% board designation right sits with his investor group, as of the annual report. Related-party arrangements, executed covenant definitions and current ownership percentages after the TopBuild share issuance are Not supplied. [CP-1A]
### Strengths and weaknesses
Strengths.

Liquidity cushion (Documentary Fact). QXO, Inc. held USD 4,704 million of liquidity at June 30, 2026, against no scheduled principal on that debt until 2030, which gives it time to integrate before a refinancing wall. [CP-1]

Maturity and rate mix (Documentary Fact). 85.9% of June 30, 2026 borrowings were fixed-rate and the earliest large maturity is USD 1,500 million in 2031, which limits both refinancing and rate pressure until the incremental term loan lifts the floating share to 42.4%. [CP-1]

Customer and demand profile (Documentary Fact; Management Language on demand). No customer exceeded 1% of net sales and management describes repair and re-roofing demand as largely non-discretionary, which supports revenue visibility but is management characterisation, not audited fact. [CP-1A]

Equity-funded growth to date (Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation on cash retention). Kodiak was paid for with preferred stock and shares, with the target's own debt repaid at closing, and common dividends are not being paid, which retained cash inside the group. [CP-1A]

Covenant headroom (Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation). The only described maintenance test is not live, with availability of USD 1,930 million against a trigger of at most USD 200 million, so covenant pressure is low until availability falls sharply. [CP-1]
Weaknesses.

Leverage unmeasured after closing (Insufficient Information). Borrowings of USD 9,111 million after the July 1, 2026 term loan have no matching reported earnings; the missing datapoints are TopBuild earnings and cash after closing, and they change every ratio. [CP-1, CP-1A]

Earnings quality (Analyst Interpretation). Add-backs make up 52.3% of Adjusted EBITDA, so management's adjusted figure depends on items that recur during integration. Last-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA margin of 7.3% sits below the 9.5% reported for FY2025, although the FY2025 base holds Beacon only from April 29, 2025. [CP-1]

Cash flow after claims (Documentary Fact). Last-twelve-month cash from operations less capital expenditures of USD 141.2 million does not cover preferred dividends paid of USD 143.8 million, and the preferred burden can rise to USD 264.1 million a year. [CP-1, CP-1A]

Integration load (Analyst Interpretation). QXO, Inc. is integrating Beacon, Kodiak and TopBuild at once with TopBuild accounting incomplete, and management's plan to more than double EBITDA is management language that no filing figure yet confirms. [CP-1A]

Concentrations and control (Documentary Fact; Insufficient Information). Three suppliers made up nearly 35% of purchases, the business reports one operating segment so no segment profit is available, and control rights are concentrated; whether control is used against creditors is not evidenced either way. [CP-1A]
### Key credit risks
| Risk | Mechanic | Credit implication | Severity |

| TopBuild and Kodiak earnings fall short of the debt and preferred claims taken on | Debt of USD 9,111 million and preferred dividends rise ahead of reported earnings; cover on current coupons is about 1.81x before the incremental loan | Leverage and debt service capacity weaken; the next decisive evidence is the third-quarter 2026 report | Critical |

| Add-backs persist rather than fade | Restructuring, transaction and transformation items recur during integration while adjusted figures exclude them | Leverage on earnings before add-backs is 17.68x; leverage tolerance is overstated if add-backs recur | Material |

| Cash call on a change of control | Series C redemption (stated value USD 3,000 million plus accrued dividends or as-converted value) and a 101% put on the notes arise from the same event | Liquidity demand at the worst moment; amounts not netted in any source | Material |

| Seasonal and working capital strain | First-quarter earnings are near nil and first-half cash from operations was negative USD 146 million | Liquidity is drawn down in the first half; relies on revolver availability and cash | Material |
| Rate exposure on the incremental term loan | Floating share rises to 42.4% of borrowings | A 100 basis point rise adds about USD 38.6 million of annual interest | Material |
| Supplier concentration and rebate dependence | Three suppliers are nearly 35% of purchases and vendor rebates reduce cost | Terms changes feed straight into gross margin | Minor |
| Change in reporting structure | New reportable segments planned after Kodiak and TopBuild with prior periods to be recast | Trend analysis breaks until recast data are published | Minor |
## Calculations
All figures are from the financial base [CP-1] unless marked; US dollars in millions.

1. Add-back share = add-backs 379.1 / LTM Adjusted EBITDA 724.8 = 52.3%. EBITDA before add-backs 345.7 / 724.8 = 47.7%. Leverage on EBITDA before add-backs: 6,111 / 345.7 = 17.68x gross and 3,337 / 345.7 = 9.65x net (CP-1 calculation 10).
2. EBITDA less capital expenditures = 724.8 - 112.2 = 612.6; over LTM cash interest 221.0 = 2.77x.
3. Cash from operations less capital expenditures, less preferred dividends paid: 141.2 - 143.8 = -2.6.

4. Fixed-rate share = (1,500 + 2,250 + 1,500) / 6,111 = 5,250 / 6,111 = 85.9%; floating 14.1%. After the incremental term loan, floating = (850 + 11 + 3,000) / 9,111 = 3,861 / 9,111 = 42.4%; fixed 5,250 / 9,111 = 57.6%. A 100 basis point rise on 3,861 = 38.6. The incremental loan is assumed floating because the filing states Term SOFR or base rate pricing.

5. Run-rate coupon on June 30, 2026 borrowings = 850 x 5.64% + 2,250 x 6.75% + 1,500 x 6.500% + 1,500 x 6.875% + 11 x 4.70% = 401.0 (CP-1 calculation 6). Cover on that run-rate = 724.8 / 401.0 = 1.81x. Illustrative: incremental term loan priced at the existing term loan rate of 5.64% (an assumption; the filing does not state the margin) = 3,000 x 5.64% = 169.2; run-rate 401.0 + 169.2 = 570.2; cover 724.8 / 570.2 = 1.27x. Both exclude interest income, commitment fees and any TopBuild earnings.
6. Illustrative earnings needed, not a covenant or target: gross leverage of 6.0x on 9,111 needs EBITDA of 1,518.5, which is 793.7 above 724.8; 5.0x needs 1,822.2, which is 1,097.4 above 724.8.

7. Secured share of borrowings after closing, assuming the incremental term loan carries the term loan's security (the filing says it is incurred under the same credit agreement): revolver 11 + term loan 850 + incremental 3,000 + 2032 notes 2,250 = 6,111, of 9,111 = 67.1%; unsecured notes 3,000 / 9,111 = 32.9%.
8. Preferred dividend ceiling 264.1 and Series C stated value 3,000 are from CP-1A calculations 4 and 5.
## Gaps
| Gap | Why it matters | Affects | Severity | Action |

| TopBuild earnings, balance sheet, debt assumed or repaid, cash acquired and purchase accounting not reported; the quarterly report says the initial accounting is incomplete (inherited from CP-1 and CP-1A) | Post-closing leverage, cover and liquidity are Not calculable; the credit view is Low confidence for the enlarged group | Assessment, key findings 1 and 3 | Critical | Obtain the third-quarter 2026 report if filed on or before 2026-11-05; otherwise keep ratios labelled pre-closing |

| Incremental term loan margin and amortisation start not stated in the pages read | Run-rate interest above 401.0 cannot be stated; the 1.27x floor rests on an assumption | Key finding 3 | Material | Obtain the July 1, 2026 amendment |

| Executed indentures, credit agreements and Series C terms not supplied | Covenant capacity, restricted payments and guarantor coverage cannot be tested; absence of creditor-adverse actions is not proof | Governance view, claims ranking | Material | Obtain exhibits listed in the June 2026 report |

| Related-party arrangements and post-issuance ownership percentages not supplied | Control and alignment cannot be assessed beyond the annual report date | Key finding 7 | Material | Obtain the proxy statement |
| Reported value of the revolver fixed charge ratio not supplied | Headroom is measured only on the availability trigger | Strength on covenant headroom | Minor | Not supplied |
| Ratings, market quotes and valuation inputs blank in the run context | No market-based view of leverage or pricing | Whole assessment | Minor | Not supplied; not treated as zero |

| Signals from CP-1A: its readiness for this module is ready with limitations, and its gap ledger carries a High gap on TopBuild accounting | Confidence is capped below High | Assessment | Material | Restated here; no further action beyond the first row |
## Next module

CP-5 (evidence review) should test the three illustrative calculations (run-rate cover, leverage break-even and secured share) against their stated assumptions, the add-back analysis, and the Insufficient Information rows, and should confirm that no recovery or relative-value conclusion has been drawn here.
